jobs.title: Program Manager, GTM Systems & Tooling
jobs.description:
About Betterment

Betterment is a leading, technology-driven financial services company that offers investing, savings and retirement solutions for retail investors and investment advisors as well as financial wellness solutions, including a 401(k) for small and medium-sized businesses. Our team is passionate about our mission, to empower people to build wealth with confidence and ease.  We’re headquartered in NYC and offer hybrid NY-based positions (four days/ week in-office, with no required office days during the summer and winter holidays).

About the Role

The Business Systems & Tooling (BS&T) team builds and operates the internal systems that power Betterment's B2B businesses — from Salesforce and its surrounding integrations to the tooling that connects our sales, service, and advisor workflows to the Betterment platform itself. Because Betterment sells across multiple lines of business, our sales tech stack has to reflect that complexity: it's not one product and one funnel, but a set of interconnected systems serving distinct teams with distinct needs.

This role owns the interface between BS&T and its stakeholders. You'll embed deeply within stakeholder teams — attending their meetings, learning their day-to-day workflows, and understanding their upcoming priorities — so that BS&T can proactively identify opportunities rather than waiting for problems to arrive as tickets. You'll then bring that context back to the team, partnering with our engineering leads and architects to translate stakeholder needs into well-scoped tasks and clear, communicated roadmaps.

This role is ideal for someone who is energized by sitting between business teams and technical teams: fluent enough in each world to be trusted by both, and disciplined enough to turn ambiguity into a plan.

This role is based out of our NYC office. Below we've reflected the base salary range for this position. Actual salaries may vary depending on factors including but not limited to location, experience, and performance. The range listed is just one component of Betterment's total compensation package for employees.

New York City: $125,000 – $145,000

This job may also be eligible for variable compensation in the form of a company incentive bonus.

A Day in the Life

Stakeholder Immersion & Discovery

- Embed with stakeholder teams across our lines of business, attending their regular meetings and building a working knowledge of their processes, tools, and pain points.

- Proactively surface opportunities for tooling improvements, automation, and best practices — bringing ideas to stakeholders rather than waiting to be handed a problem.

- Maintain a continuously updated view of each stakeholder group's upcoming priorities and how they map to BS&T's capacity and roadmap.

- Act as the first point of contact for new stakeholder requests, gathering context and framing the underlying need before work is committed.

Scoping, Roadmapping & Prioritization

- Partner with BS&T's engineering lead and architects to translate stakeholder needs into scoped, documented tasks with clear success criteria.

- Own and communicate the BS&T roadmap, making prioritization decisions legible to stakeholders and aligning our planning rhythm with the rest of the company.

- Balance urgent stakeholder priorities against high-value quality-of-life improvements, ensuring compounding wins don't get perpetually deferred.

- Run intake, backlog grooming, and status communication processes so the team's work — and the reasoning behind it — is visible.

Vendor & Salestech Landscape

- Stay current on the salestech landscape, evaluating emerging tools and practices for fit with Betterment's stack.

- Support vendor assessments, procurement, and renewal processes across our salestech vendors, partnering with Finance, Legal, and Security as needed.

- Help stakeholders evaluate build-vs-buy tradeoffs with a clear-eyed view of total cost, integration complexity, and maintenance burden.

What We're Looking For

Skills & Experience

- 5+ years of experience in product management, technical program management, business systems analysis, or a similar role sitting between business stakeholders and technical teams.

- Working knowledge of Salesforce and the surrounding GTM systems ecosystem (e.g., CPQ workflows, enrichment, engagement, and integration tooling) — enough to scope work credibly and ask the right questions, even if you don't build in it yourself.

- Experience at a company with a complex, multi-product go-to-market — where internal systems must integrate the CRM, adjacent salestech tools, and the product being sold itself.

- Demonstrated ability to turn ambiguous stakeholder requests into scoped, prioritized, well-documented work.

- Experience supporting vendor evaluation, procurement, or renewal processes is a strong plus.

Professional Competencies

- Builds trust quickly with both business stakeholders and engineers, and communicates fluently with each in their own terms.

- Comfortable saying "not yet" — able to make prioritization tradeoffs transparent and keep stakeholder confidence even when their request isn't next.

- Proactive by default: identifies opportunities and proposes solutions rather than operating purely on intake.

- Strong writer and documenter; believes that a decision isn't made until it's written down and shared.

- Thrives in a small team where process is yours to design, not inherited.

Nice to Have

- Experience in fintech, financial services, or another regulated industry.

- Familiarity with SQL or data analysis tools sufficient to self-serve answers about system and business data.

- Exposure to marketing automation or martech platforms (e.g., Braze, HubSpot).

Join a team built on these core values

We change lives

Be a part of a community of innovators working to transform financial outcomes for real people. Your work will make an impact, always laddering up to our mission; to empower people to build wealth with confidence and ease .

We set audacious goals

We set them for the company, our customers, and ourselves, and we won’t stop until we reach them. We don’t just show up; we give our all, then celebrate our wins.

We value all perspectives

When we collaborate, we're at our best. We believe diverse perspectives lead to better outcomes and strive to uphold our supportive and inclusive community.

We simplify financial services

We’re financial services pioneers, always finding new ways to improve, optimize, and enhance. Constant improvement is in our DNA.

Our Commitment to Your Total Well-being:

- We offer a competitive suite of benefits , including medical, dental, and vision coverage; life and AD&D insurance; short- and long-term disability; infertility support and WPATH-aligned transgender health benefits; an Employee Assistance Program (EAP); transit benefits and FSA and HSA options

- Ownership: Equity for all employees, including new hire and refresher grants.

- Time: Flexible paid time off, paid parental leave, and a fully paid four-week sabbatical in your sixth year.

- Growth: Company-paid professional coaching for all employees.

- Wealth: Day-one 401(k) match plus matching on qualified student loan payments.

What happens next

We’ll take a few weeks to review all applications. If we’d like to spend more time with you, we’ll reach out to arrange next steps, which will include 3-4 sets of meetings with your future colleagues.

In the interview process, we’ll look to learn more about your skills, experiences, capabilities, and motivators. Many of our questions will be aimed at understanding how you might operate here at Betterment. Depending on the role, we may ask you to complete a case study exercise or technical assessments, as we want to collect a robust set of data points to better inform our decisions.

On average, it takes us around 3-5 weeks to make a hiring decision, depending on your availability and sense of urgency. As a best practice, we aim to interview at least 2-3 final round candidates before making a hiring decision. jobs.title: Revenue Operations Manager - Revenue Planning & Insights
jobs.description:
About Betterment

Betterment is a leading, technology-driven financial services company that offers investing, savings and retirement solutions for retail investors and investment advisors as well as financial wellness solutions, including a 401(k) for small and medium-sized businesses. Our team is passionate about our mission, to empower people to build wealth with confidence and ease.  We’re headquartered in NYC and offer hybrid NY-based positions (four days/ week in-office, with no required office days during the summer and winter holidays).

About the Role

We're hiring an analyst and builder for our Revenue Operations team to be a force multiplier for our go-to-market organization. Sometimes that means tackling a question with no playbook yet. Sometimes it means running an established process and improving it as you go.

You'll take on ambiguous, high impact questions and turn them into clearly defined problems, design the right solution, and drive it through build, adoption, and continuous improvement.

The role has three modes. First, you'll drive the analytical core: forecasting, executive reporting, revenue planning, QBR-grade analyses over large datasets, quota and target analytics, and the models that support forecasting and planning. You'll present your own work directly to leadership and translate complex business questions into actionable insights.

Second, you'll build net-new systems: internal tools, data models, and reporting infrastructure that teammates then run and scale. That includes planning models, dashboards, and operational workflows that make the business more efficient over time.

Third, you'll make Revenue Operations more leveraged with AI, whether that's building AI-assisted tooling, designing account scoring and research logic in our go-to-market stack, or automating work that shouldn't be manual. You’ll constantly look for more opportunities to increase leverage across the organization.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical horsepower with a systems mindset and genuine comfort with ambiguity. You ask why until you understand the business objective behind a request, you design solutions that scale beyond the first use case, and you already use AI to build and move faster than your job title suggests. You’re naturally curious about how AI can improve the way work gets done, but you know technology is only valuable when it solves a real business problem. And you finish: to you, work is done when it's adopted, documented, and running without you, not when the analysis is shipped.

This role is based out of our NYC office.

- New York City: $120,000 - $160,000

- Build and continuously improve our reporting engine end to end, from the data models and infrastructure underneath to the reporting and forecasting rhythms that help leadership understand business performance, risks, and opportunities. When an issue traces back to upstream CRM design, process, or data quality, partner with the right teams to fix it at the source.

- Own QBR processes, including analyses using large, complex datasets and present your findings and recommendations directly to go-to-market leadership.

- Contribute to revenue planning, quota and target setting: including capacity-based quota analysis, attainment and distribution analysis, and repeatable quarterly target-update processes.

- Investigate complex business questions with no established playbook. You'll determine the right data, methodology, and level of analysis needed to produce a decision-ready answer.

- Build internal tools using AI-assisted development, balancing speed with accuracy, maintainability, and security without over-engineering.

- Architect solutions you may not build yourself: translate business problems into clear requirements, decision logic, and success criteria, then drive execution with Business Systems, Data Engineering, and other partner teams.

What We're Looking For:

- At least five years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Go-to-Market Analytics, or Business Operations, or a highly analytical operating role.

- Investigate open-ended business questions, determining the right data, methodology, and solution.

- SQL fluency and comfort handling large, intricate datasets – you think in joins, grain, and systems of record.

- A systems mindset: you anticipate edge cases, understand downstream impacts, and design scalable solutions that won’t need to be rebuilt every quarter.

- Fluency with  modern AI tools to accelerate analysis, problem-solving, and development – ou're comfortable working with agentic AI workflows, critically evaluating outputs, and choosing the right solution for the problem

- Strong analytical instincts and business judgment – you optimize for the objective behind the ask, not the ask itself.

- Executive-ready communication skills – you can confidently present your own analysis to senior leadership.

- Experience supporting forecasting, revenue planning, quota planning, executive reporting, or other core Revenue Operations planning processes.

- Hands-on experience working with Salesforce data — reports, objects, and the data structures underneath them.

- Experience building reporting and dashboards with BI tools such as Tableau.
